title: AMECEA: AMECEA Set to Launch Formation Manual, New Songs on Synodality
desc:
Sr. Jecinter Antoinette Okoth, FSSA
The Association of Member Episcopal Conferences in Eastern Africa (AMECEA), through its Social Communications department, will launch a Formation Synodality Manual (a training handbook) and a collection of new songs on Synodality to deepen the Church's synodal journey across the region.
The hybrid event will take place on Thursday, March 12. For the onsite participants, the launch will be at Donum Dei, Roussel house, in Kenya’s capital, Nairobi.  Virtual participants can join the session using the link provided:
https://youtube.com/live/VU3GWQcyGio?feature=share
As AMECEA prepares for this great day, having a synodality training manual and synodality songs in the region will help in the implementation phase, which “aims to examine new practices and structures that will make the life of the Church more synodal, starting from the overall perspective outlined in the Final Document (FD), with a view to more effectively carrying out the mission of evangelisation.”
The synodality manual will be a training tool for different groups in the region on synodality. It will therefore give parishes, Small Christian Communities (SCC), and dioceses a structured, accessible tool for understanding and living the synodal way of being a Church.
Besides, as the Synod on Synodality directed the universal Church on journeying together as a way, the formation manual will also help sustain the synodal momentum of communion, participation, and mission.
Other than the formation document, AMECEA piloted three conferences in Tanzania, Malawi, and Zambia to compose synodality songs. These songs aim to help the people of God internalize values such as listening, walking together, and discernment in ways that the formation manual alone cannot fully accomplish. Other member conferences in the region will also be involved.
So far, Monze Diocese in Zambia has composed and launched 10 synodality songs; Malawi and Tanzania have three songs each, ready for Thursday's launch.  Some of these songs will be played to participants on the day of the launch, while radios across the AMECEA region will continue to play them.
The launch, therefore, marks a significant step in equipping Catholic and non-Catholic communities with practical tools for formation and liturgical expression as the Church continues to walk together in the spirit of Synodality.
